Nobody wants to say it, but here it is:
Australia's deadliest terror attack since forever happened because of a chain of massive, glaring failures. 15 innocent people slaughtered at a Hanukkah celebration. 

A 10-year-old girl. A rabbi with a newborn baby. Holocaust survivors. Families lighting candles for joy – turned into a bloodbath.
The attackers: Father Sajid Akram (50, shot dead by police) and son Naveed Akram (24, critical in hospital under guard). Motivated by ISIS ideology. Used Sajid's legally owned firearms – he had a license for six guns, was a gun club member.

The timeline that exposes the rot:
1998: Sajid arrives on student visa, later gets residency.

2019: Naveed investigated by ASIO for ties to a Sydney ISIS cell. On radar, but no charges.

After 2019: Sajid keeps/renews gun licenses. No red flag from son's probe

Nov 2025: Father-son duo travel to Philippines (island with Islamist insurgency) – possible training.

Dec 14, 2025: They target "Chanukah by the Sea" on Bondi. Fire from footbridge. 15 dead, 40+ injured.

Ignored warnings everywhere:
Antisemitic incidents exploding since Oct 2023: Synagogue arsons, attacks, protests.
ASIO raised threat level to "probable" in 2024 over Gaza tensions.

July 2025 antisemitism envoy report: Recommendations to fight hate – mostly unimplemented.
Yet licenses stayed valid. No family scrutiny. Hate allowed to fester.
Albanese's response? Gun law tweaks (caps, stricter checks). Sure, needed – but the guns were ALREADY legal and registered. The problem isn't just weapons; it's who gets them when red flags are waving.

This wasn't random. It was systemic blindness: Weak vetting on residency paths. No license revocation post-terror probe. Ignoring rising extremism to avoid "racism" accusations.

The real hero: Ahmed al-Ahmed, 43-year-old Muslim dad and local shop owner. Tackled a gunman, wrestled away the rifle while getting shot multiple times. Saved countless lives. Fundraiser hit $1M+. Proves it's not about religion – it's about radicals vs. decent people.

Netanyahu wasn't wrong calling out the "cancer cells" allowed to grow.
The pattern repeats in the West: Mass immigration without real integration demands. Ignore signs. Suppress debate. Shock when violence hits.

We owe Matilda, Rabbi Schlanger, and the 13 others better. Demand answers: Why no action after 2019 probe? Why no follow-up on Philippines trip? Why shelve antisemitism fixes?

Light beats darkness – but only if we face the failures head-on.
RIP to the victims. Strength to families. Eternal thanks to heroes like Ahmed.

Sources: ABC, SMH, Reuters, NYT, BBC, official statements.

WATCH: Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon says at least three out of the four pumps at the controversial Sunog Apog pumping station in Manila should be operational before the rainy season in 2026. 

The P774-million flood control facility was completed in 2020 during the Duterte administration, but was found dysfunctional and said to have worsened flooding.

The project was supposed to address flooding in Manila such as España, Sampaloc, Rizal Ave., and Maria Clara. | @bylancemejico 
 
📹 DPWH
